instruction.text: This formula describes how many sandwiches, 𝘴, are needed to feed a number of people, 𝘱.

atoms.a: How many sandwiches are needed to feed 10 people?
How many sandwiches are needed to feed 8 people?

instruction.text: Lisa uses this formula to find out how many minutes, 𝘮, she needs to make a number of pizzas, 𝘱.

atoms.a: How many minutes does she need to make 4 pizzas?
How many minutes does she need to make 9 pizzas?

instruction.text: Mary uses this formula to find out her earnings, E, from selling a number of books, 𝘣, at a price of £20.

atoms.a: How much does Mary make if she sells 100 copies?
How much does Mary make if she sells 25 copies?

instruction.text: A teacher uses this formula to calculate how many pens, 𝘱, she needs to buy for a class with a number of students, 𝘴.

atoms.a: How many pens does she need to buy if her class has 23 pupils?
How many pens does she need to buy if her class has 12 pupils?

instruction.text: This formula describes the time, 𝘵, it takes for an artist to draw a number of sketches, 𝘯.

atoms.a: How many minutes does it take to draw 7 sketches?
How many minutes does it take to draw 11 sketches?
